newsitem.title: USA: Broin attorney doubts tobacco's view on settlement.
newsitem.headline: Broin attorney doubts tobacco's view on settlement.

text.p: Stanley Rosenblatt, the attorney representing plaintiffs in a landmark anti-tobacco class action suit, said Friday he doubted contentions by tobacco industry attorneys that a broad settlement agreement between the industry and state officials would not affect the case.
"I'm not comfortable (with their contention)," Rosenblatt said after a morning of jury selection in the case known as Norma Broin vs. Philip Morris Cos Inc et al.

In the case, thousands of non-smoking flight attendants are suing cigarette makers seeking redress for illnesses, including lung cancer, that they said are linked to breathing second-hand smoke on U.S.-based passenger jets. It is the first second-hand smoke case and first class action against big tobacco to make it to trial.

Before jury selection began a 12th day Friday, attorneys representing Philip Morris, R.J. Reynolds Tobacco Co, Brown & Williamson Tobacco Corp and Lorillard Tobacco Co said their client companies did not expect the industrywide settlement being negotiated in Washington to wipe out the landmark class action.

The attorneys made statements in opposing a motion by Rosenblatt and his wife, Susan, also an attorney for the plaintiffs, that Dade County Circuit Judge Robert Kaye issue an order that a settlement agreement would not stop the Broin case from going forward.
Rosenblatt said the tobacco attorneys' opposition to the motion was not consistent with a belief that cigarette firms would not try to use a settlement to have the Broin case thrown out of court.
"Why wouldn't they agree to that if they're saying this case is going forward? So no, I'm not comfortable with that (contention)," Rosenblatt said.
